composition.story: A parent node holds 6 A and 4 B samples. A split sends them into two children. Compute each node's Gini impurity, average the children by size, then subtract from the parent. That drop is the information gain.

aha.observation: Information gain is the parent's Gini minus the size-weighted average of the children's Gini. A bigger drop means a better split.

controls.label: Split
controls.presentation: Selects which variant of the split is shown; changes child counts and every computed value.

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Returns to the first state and the default split.

states.label: Parent
states.sentence: Parent proportions are 0.6 and 0.4, so Gini = 1 − (0.36 + 0.16) = 0.48.
states.why: Gini = 1 − sum of squared class proportions.

states.label: Split
states.sentence: The split sends 5 samples left and 5 right. Each child keeps its own class counts.
states.why: Child sizes become the weights later.

states.label: Left Gini
states.sentence: Left proportions are 0.8 and 0.2, so Gini = 1 − (0.64 + 0.04) = 0.32.
states.why: Same formula, applied to the left counts only.

states.label: Right Gini
states.sentence: Right proportions are 0.4 and 0.6, so Gini = 1 − (0.16 + 0.36) = 0.48.
states.why: Same formula, applied to the right counts only.

states.label: Weighted
states.sentence: Weight each child by its share of samples: 0.5 × 0.32 + 0.5 × 0.48 = 0.40.
states.why: Larger children count more toward the average.

states.label: Gain
states.sentence: Information gain = parent Gini − weighted child Gini = 0.48 − 0.40 = 0.08.
states.why: The impurity removed by the split.

states.label: Parent
states.sentence: Parent proportions are 0.6 and 0.4, so Gini = 1 − (0.36 + 0.16) = 0.48.
states.why: Gini = 1 − sum of squared class proportions.

states.label: Split
states.sentence: The split sends 4 samples left and 6 right. Each child keeps its own class counts.
states.why: Child sizes become the weights later.

states.label: Left Gini
states.sentence: Left proportions are 1.0 and 0.0, so Gini = 1 − (1 + 0) = 0. The node is pure.
states.why: Same formula, applied to the left counts only.

states.label: Right Gini
states.sentence: Right proportions are 0.33 and 0.67, so Gini = 1 − (0.111 + 0.444) = 0.444.
states.why: Same formula, applied to the right counts only.

states.label: Weighted
states.sentence: Weight each child by its share of samples: 0.4 × 0 + 0.6 × 0.444 = 0.267.
states.why: Larger children count more toward the average.

states.label: Gain
states.sentence: Information gain = parent Gini − weighted child Gini = 0.48 − 0.267 = 0.213.
states.why: The impurity removed by the split; larger than Split X.
